stem: Before filling Fycompa, profile review shows an issue date five months ago and three of five refills used. Select every correct conclusion.

choices.text: The federal six-month issue-date deadline still applies.
Stable seizure control permits indefinite refills.
A new prescription is required after every fill because it is Schedule II.
Covered Schedule III dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: The federal six-month issue-date deadline still applies. Covered Schedule III dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.

choice_analysis.A: Supported: The federal six-month issue-date deadline still applies.
choice_analysis.B: Not supported: Stable seizure control permits indefinite refills.
choice_analysis.C: Not supported: Antiseizure use makes Fycompa noncontrolled.
choice_analysis.D: Not supported: A new prescription is required after every fill because it is Schedule II.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Covered Schedule III dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.

related_facts: perampanel (Fycompa) is used for treatment of partial-onset seizures and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures; it is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.

Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Stable seizure control permits indefinite refills.'

reasoning_steps: Classify perampanel under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
Match the scenario's operative facts to Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits
